strings.name: Julio Ponce Lerou
strings.role: Chilean businessman and former SQM chairman
strings.summary: Julio Ponce Lerou is a Chilean forestry engineer and businessman who held public-sector positions under Pinochet and later led SQM's board for many years. Through layered holding companies, he participated in mining investment; his career involves privatization, family succession and the Cascadas securities-trading controversy.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Board roles and ownership, announced and completed restructuring, and administrative fines and civil claims are distinguished; dismissal of specific claims is not described as acquittal in all cases.
strings.influence.rationale: Long involved in SQM governance and Chile's lithium industry, influencing global battery-material supply and corporate-governance debate.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Forestry engineer trained at Universidad de Chile; no precise graduation year or additional degree is inferred.
strings.facts.f2.label: Roles and family succession
strings.facts.f2.value: He left SQM's board in 2015 and announced in 2025 that future management and family asset matters would pass to his family, represented by his daughter Francisca.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Mining and holding structures
strings.highlights.h1.text: He participated in SQM through holding companies over many years; its businesses include lithium, iodine and nitrates, and company output cannot be attributed entirely to one individual.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Securities regulation and civil litigation
strings.highlights.h2.text: The Cascadas case involved administrative fines and separate civil claims; reducing the fine and dismissing compensation claims were different proceedings.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Pension funds' civil claims dismissed
strings.timeline.t1.text: Cooperativa reported that the Supreme Court rejected challenges from three pension fund administrators, leaving the denial of compensation in place.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Announces family management handover
strings.timeline.t2.text: A written statement assigned future management and asset matters to the family, represented by Francisca; this did not mean all shares had been sold.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Administrative fine review reported
strings.timeline.t3.text: A public legal summary said the Supreme Court upheld the fine reduced to 75,000 UF; the reduction did not overturn all findings of infringements.
strings.timeline.t4.title: SQM chairmanship ends
strings.timeline.t4.text: He chaired his final shareholders' meeting in that role and left the board, while retaining ownership influence at the time.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Administrative sanction in Cascadas case
strings.timeline.t5.text: The securities regulator imposed a fine for infringements involving share transactions; its amount later underwent judicial review.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Reelection at Soquimich Comercial
strings.timeline.t6.text: The 2013 annual report lists him as chairman and records this latest reelection date; the company is distinct from parent SQM.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Returns to SQM
strings.timeline.t7.text: He returned during privatization, beginning the later chairmanship that continued until 2015.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Becomes head of Conaf
strings.timeline.t8.text: He took a leadership role at the national forestry agency during military rule; he was then related to the Pinochet family by marriage.
